summary: This June 2025 Iran-war update extends the 2024 Iran Trap into a live-field model: regime change means destroying national capacity, bombs-propaganda-money may fail against Iran, strategic flexibility beats dominance, and no-nuke, ground-war, China-restraint, assassination, and civil-war-trigger branches need split Prediction handling.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Iran pressure does not stay local: U.S. regime-change methods, Iranian identity, Hormuz, Gulf clients, American bases, consumer prices, and domestic support all move together.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The existing Iran pressure lens already owns transmission across invasion logic, Hormuz, Gulf protection, dollar/order pressure, and morale. This source is a chronology bridge from the 2024 trap formulation into the live June 2025 war field, but no episode read JSON link is changed in this intake.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Jiang says America has overwhelming military power, but Iran has more strategic flexibility because it can choose wider pain surfaces and sustain costs differently.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Strategy page already carries dominance-versus-control and escalation-control anchors. This source gives an earlier Iran-war field application of the same rule without needing a new standalone Control Beats Dominance page.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The June 18, 2025 update names several forecast branches that must stay separate before ledger scoring: imminent bombing, no nuclear use, Supreme Leader assassination, Putin's ground-war trap, China restraint, draft, and American civil-war pressure.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Prediction owns source date, branch split, later comparison, and possible miss/revision. This source should feed the Iran active-watch family, not become a broad 'Jiang predicted Iran war' ledger item.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold as a June 18, 2025 live-field continuation after the May 29, 2024 Iran Trap: Jiang now treats imminent bombing as likely and says the U.S. regime-change toolkit will not work cleanly because Iran's geography, Persian civilizational identity, prior observation of Iraq, Hormuz/Gulf vulnerability, and base exposure turn pressure on Tehran into system pressure.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Iran As Pressure Point owns the transmission surface. Chokepoint owns strait/access mechanics, Strategy owns material-war control versus dominance, Nation owns general population-as-capacity only when the national-machine mechanism is primary, and Prediction owns dated branch status.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this source as an earlier regime-change and control-versus-dominance bridge: 'bombs, propaganda, money' and leadership decapitation are tested against terrain, morale, decentralized cells, supply lines, sunk cost, and consumer/political will.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Strategy owns the material audit: whether the regime-change story survives geography, organization, morale, supply, duration, and enemy adaptation. Stories/Legitimacy Fiction would own only the propaganda surface if the active mechanism were narrative legitimacy rather than war performance.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the source as a June 2025 no-exit/chokepoint predecessor: Iran's ability to close Hormuz, strike desalination/oil fields, hit regional bases, and force high oil prices creates exit cost before any full occupation branch begins.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Chokepoint receives the access-control and Gulf-client exposure surfaces. No-Exit War receives sunk cost, ground troops, and black-hole occupation logic. Iran As Pressure Point remains the broader transmission home.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Queue separate dated forecast branches from this 2025-06-18 update: imminent U.S. bombing, no nuclear weapons absent very high escalation, Supreme Leader assassination as an unknown, Putin using silence to lure a ground invasion, American draft/civil-war pressure, and China staying mostly restrained despite oil dependence.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Prediction owns the dated claims and comparison surface. It should not count all Iran-war developments as one hit, nor should it merge this June 2025 source into the later March-April 2026 active-watch family without preserving the earlier formulation.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Record as a method source: Jiang explicitly says he is using game theory to predict war contours and wants to teach the audience to map incentives, pain surfaces, and player constraints rather than react to headlines.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns the player/incentive map and the claim that apparent restraint or silence can be strategic. Prediction owns whether the resulting forecasts later hold.

new_lens_seeds.title: Regime Change Destroys National Capacity
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Jiang defines regime change as destroying the society's capacity to function collectively as a nation through leadership decapitation, infrastructure/sanctions pressure, opposition financing, and sectarian fragmentation.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare Iraq, Libya, Syria, Iran, and later hybrid-war sources where infrastructure and legitimacy pressure target the state-population bond rather than only the government.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a comparison seed only. Current public homes can carry the mechanism: Strategy's hybrid-war/state-bond section, Iran As Pressure Point, and Nation only when national capacity as population machinery becomes primary. Do not create a standalone Regime Change page from this source alone.

chronology_notes.note: On 2025-06-18 Jiang moves from the 2024 Iran Trap exercise into a live-war update: U.S. bombing is expected soon, but Iran's terrain, identity, observation of Iraq, Hormuz leverage, Gulf client exposure, and base network make regime-change pressure transmit through the wider system.

The 2025-06-18 source is an earlier field application of the later control-over-dominance rule: America has military dominance, but Iran may have strategic flexibility through geography, morale, decentralized cells, Gulf vulnerabilities, oil prices, and U.S. domestic will.

This source predates the March-April 2026 active-watch cluster and should be preserved as a June 2025 branch set, not flattened into later claims. It names no-nuke reasoning, assassination uncertainty, Putin's ground-war trap, draft/civil-war pressure, and China-restraint expectations.
